cards.text: Ezekiel the prophet gets another word from the LORD, and friend, there's no small talk in this one. God calls him son of man and asks him a question. Will he pass judgment on the city of bloodshed?

cards.question: God asks Ezekiel if he'll pass judgment on the city of bloodshed. Then what does God tell him to do with her?

answers.text: Confront her with all her abominations
Comfort her in all her troubles
Remind her of all her victories

cards.text: Here's what the Lord GOD says to the city. She's bringing her own doom on herself, friend, and two things are doing it.

cards.question: The city brings her own doom by shedding ___ within her walls and making ___ to defile herself.

cards.text: God says she's guilty of the blood she's shed, and she's brought her days to a close. Now the other nations are watching.

cards.question: God says the city's days are at an end. How will the lands near and far treat her?

cards.text: Near AND far, friend, that's not one group chat laughing at you, that's EVERY group chat. Then God gets specific: every prince of Israel in her has used his power to shed blood.

cards.question: Inside the city of bloodshed, father and mother are still treated with honor. True or false?
Within the city's walls, the foreign resident is exploited. Who else is oppressed there?

cards.text: And it's not just how they treat people. It's how they treat what belongs to God.

cards.question: The city has despised God's holy things and ___ His Sabbaths.

cards.text: The list keeps going: slanderous men bent on bloodshed, people eating at the mountain shrines, and men sinning against their neighbor's wife and their own families.
Then the money comes in: bribes to shed blood, excess interest, extorting the neighbors. Friend, this city would charge you a fee just for asking about the fees.

cards.question: After all the bribes and extortion, God says one more thing. He says they have ___ Him.

cards.text: Now God strikes His hands together against their unjust gain and the blood they've shed. Then He asks if her courage will hold on the day He deals with her.

cards.question: God says He has spoken about the city, but He'll wait and see before He acts. True or false?
Now God tells the city what's coming. What will He do with her people?

answers.text: Hide them up in the mountains
Send them all back to Egypt

cards.text: Scattered throughout the lands. And God says He'll purge her uncleanness.

cards.question: Once the city has defiled herself in the eyes of the nations, what does God say she will know?

cards.text: Then the word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel again. This time God pictures the house of Israel inside a furnace.

cards.question: God pictures the house of Israel inside a furnace. What does He say they've become to Him?
Because they've all become dross, God says He'll gather them into one city. Which one?

cards.text: All of them copper, tin, iron and lead, the dross of silver, and I thought getting tossed in a junk drawer was rough! Just like metal gets gathered into a furnace to melt with a fiery blast, God will gather them in His anger and wrath.

cards.question: God says He'll gather them into the furnace and then pull them right back out. True or false?

cards.text: Then God says it again. He'll gather them, blow on them with the fire of His wrath, and they'll be melted within the city.

cards.question: God says they'll be melted within the city, like silver in a furnace. Then what will they know the LORD has done?

answers.text: Poured out His wrath on them
Turned all of them into silver

cards.text: Then another word from the LORD comes. Ezekiel is to tell the land that in the day of indignation, she hasn't been cleansed and no rain has fallen on her.
Now God goes down the list of who's in charge, starting with the princes. Their conspiracy is like a roaring lion tearing its prey.

cards.question: The princes devour the people, seize the treasures and multiply the ___ within the land.
Next God turns to the priests. They do violence to His law and make no distinction between the holy and the ___.

cards.text: Then come the officials, and they're no better. They're like wolves tearing their prey, destroying lives for dishonest gain.

cards.question: The princes, the priests and the officials are all doing harm. What do the land's prophets do with these deeds?

answers.text: Hide away from them in the hills

cards.text: They even say, “This is what the Lord GOD says,” when the LORD has not spoken. That's like sending a memo with your boss's name on it that your boss NEVER wrote.

cards.question: With the leaders like this, at least the everyday people of the land are treating the poor and needy fairly. True or false?

cards.text: Then God says He searched for a man among them to repair the wall and stand in the gap before Him on behalf of the land, so that He should not destroy it.

cards.question: God searched for someone to stand in the gap for the land. How many did He find?

cards.text: So God pours out His indignation on them and brings their ways down on their own heads. Heavy word, friend, and you stayed with it all the way to the end.

findings.problem: The card says men are "sinning against their neighbor's wife." Ezekiel 22:11 says a man "commits an abomination with his neighbor's wife." Changing "with" to "against" makes her a victim, which the text doesn't say. Use the text's word, for example "men committing abominations with their neighbor's wife."

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Polished bronze" is close to the passage. Ezekiel 22:18 says the house of Israel is "copper, tin, iron, and lead inside the furnace." Bronze is a copper alloy, so a baker could argue that "bronze" fits. Replace it with a metal the passage never uses for Israel.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: This story card comes after card 3, which already asked about Ezekiel 22:19. It then goes back to retell 22:18 (copper, tin, iron and lead, the dross of silver), which card 2 already covered. This is a step backward and a partial recap, not a step forward. The 22:18 metals detail should go before cards 2 and 3, and this card should start at 22:20.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
